reviewer.notes: Every headline count in the receipt reproduced exactly on a fresh live re-run of all three named probes, and -- more importantly -- on independently-written re-implementations that do not import the implementer's summarizer/comparator code (hand-typed osv-scanner target list + standalone dedup script for probe1; direct `gh api` calls bypassing probe2's helper functions). I specifically tried several distinct falsification angles: shared summarizer bug, fabricated 403, fabricated Advisory-DB counts, sample-cap cherry-picking (checked the one package the 15-cap silently excluded and found it would have corroborated too), inflated affected_package_count from the repo's documented skills/ vs .agents/skills/ duplicate file and cross-project duplicate npm packages, and an apparent severity-sum/vuln-id-count mismatch (58 vs 77, explained by 34 ids lacking a severity field). None of these broke a claimed headline number; the affected_package_count and severity-sum items are documented here as legitimate methodological nuances (occurrence-count vs distinct-identity; partial severity coverage) rather than falsifications, since the receipt's own method fields already describe the counting convention used and never claim the alternate interpretation. I did not promote the receipt; state=BLOCKED and reviewer.verdict=NOT-REVIEWED remain exactly as found on disk, and I reverted the timestamp-only diffs my probe re-runs produced before writing this review artifact so the branch stays clean. This independent-review.json is a separate artifact for a downstream packer step (not run by me) to consult when deciding whether to promote the receipt.
